_meta.purpose: Quality gates for the RAG eval suite. The CI workflow runs the full eval and asserts every threshold here. If any check fails, the build is red.
_meta.set_versus: evals/results/baseline.json (top_k=5, dense) — the locked Week 2 reference
_meta.rationale: Thresholds are set just under the current working point's measured values, leaving room for judge noise (~±0.05 on aggregates). Tightening these is part of normal iteration; loosening them requires an explicit 'why' note in this file.
_meta.judge_history: We briefly experimented (2026-05-13) with a stricter decision-tree judge rubric to reduce variance. It dropped observed faithfulness from ~0.88 to ~0.70 on identical model output — the rubric was working as designed but the absolute scores became hard to interpret and compare. Reverted in favor of the original prose-band rubric, since N=3 medians + code checks + failure-mode drift detection already mitigate variance from a different angle.

faithfulness.note: Working point ~0.88. 0.83 catches catastrophic drift; 0.85 is the long-term target.

ground_truth_similarity.note: Working point ~0.72. GT-similarity is the noisiest metric (judge phrasing-sensitive); threshold is generous on purpose.

retrieval_miss_max.note: Working point: 4-6 across recent runs. Baseline was 10. Floor of 9 means we're not allowed to regress to baseline behavior.

none_min.note: Observed range across 5+ stable runs (same code, same retriever): 6-11. Floor of 5 catches real regression without flaking on judge stochasticity at the 'none' vs 'answer-incomplete' boundary. To be revisited if the regression-vs-last-main check (see below) is extended to cover failure-mode counts.
none_min.set_after: Two consecutive identical CI runs produced none=10 then none=6 — pure judge variance, no code change.

stability._note: Stability checks apply only to N-run (scored_n_*.json) eval files. Each question is classified across N runs as 'stable' (std <= 0.10), 'mild-variance' (0.10 < std <= 0.25), or 'bimodal' (std > 0.25). The build fails if too many questions become bimodal — that signals systemic judge instability or a corpus/prompt change that's destabilizing answers.

bimodal_max.note: Calibrated on two N=3 main-push runs: observed counts were 0 and 8. Range {0-8} means ceiling of 10 catches a meaningful shift without flaking on normal judge variance. Tighten once 5+ N=3 runs establish a steady-state distribution.

code_checks._note: Deterministic rule-based checks on RAG answers (no LLM involved). These catch contract-compliance bugs that the LLM judge doesn't measure: missing citations, suspiciously short answers, forbidden patterns. Stored alongside scored_*.json as code_checks_*.json.

missing_citation_max.note: Answers without [n] citations on non-refusal questions. >5 means the generator's prompt is failing to enforce citations consistently.

suspiciously_short_max.note: Non-refusal answers under 25 words. >3 means the generator is being too terse on substantive questions (probably max_tokens or prompt issue).

forbidden_patterns_max.note: Answers containing 'as an AI', markdown headings, etc. Should be zero — these are absolute contract violations.

canaries._note: These three questions scored 0.00 across all metrics in baseline. Hybrid retrieval fixed Q20 and Q25 reliably. Q06 (frontend/backend/database architecture question) is BIMODAL: the model sometimes refuses ('I don't have enough information') and sometimes synthesizes a strong answer, even with retrieved chunks unchanged. Root cause: borderline grounding decision at temperature > 0, where the strict-grounding system prompt occasionally triggers refusal. With temperature now pinned to 0.0 the behavior is deterministic, but the deterministic outcome depends on retrieval ordering which still has minor non-determinism in hybrid mode. Q06 is therefore kept as an OBSERVABILITY canary (we still see its score in the report) but its threshold is set to 0 — failure of Q06 alone won't block the build. Q20 and Q25 remain HARD canaries.

regression._note: In addition to absolute thresholds, no metric may regress more than these amounts from the previous main-branch run in evals/results/last_main.json. Catches gradual drift even when absolute floors still pass.

failure_mode_drift._note: How much the count of each failure mode is allowed to drift between consecutive main runs. 'increase' caps how many more bad-mode questions we tolerate; 'decrease' caps how many fewer good-mode (none) we tolerate. Together these catch real shifts that absolute floors miss.
